item.subject: maths
item.stem:
The diagram shows lines $PQ$ and $RS$ cut by transversal $AC$. Triangles $PAC$ and $RCA$ are congruent, and that congruence makes one pair of alternate interior angles equal.

Which claim correctly concludes that $PQ \parallel RS$?

options.A: $PQ \parallel RS$, because the congruent triangles make a pair of alternate interior angles equal for transversal $AC$.
options.B: Lines $PQ$ and $RS$ are the alternate interior angles on transversal $AC$.
options.C: $PQ \parallel RS$, because the triangles are congruent, even when those alternate interior angles are unequal.
options.D: $PQ \parallel RS$, because matching sides of the triangles are equal, and equal sides alone settle parallelism.
